paragraphs.dominant_move: threat-and-objective: Debris creates collision exposure and a potential private-service opportunity. -> sets the decision target -> defines the firm and model chain
firm-and-architecture: A merged insurer-remover allows one accounting model to connect premiums, removal, and collision losses. -> defines the modeled decision maker -> opens the profit model
economic-model: Annual revenue and two cost classes can represent time-dependent commercial performance. -> creates the financial output -> requests collision probability
collision-model: A Gamma-filled matrix and repeated random placement are used to estimate collision frequency. -> supplies Pr(t) and Q_t -> moves to policy
policy-model: A two-player matrix can compare behavior before and after regulation. -> creates an equilibrium claim -> combines decisions
parameter-boundary: Commercial conclusions depend materially on the insurance rate and the no-discounting assumption. -> qualifies transfer -> states recommendations
decision: The combined alternative, a sufficient commission, and an industrial standard are recommended. -> closes the compact argument -> the executive summary expands it
hazard-context: Debris scale and collision consequences make removal consequential. -> establishes demand -> asks about implementation
commercial-question: The unresolved issue is whether removal can be implemented as a viable service. -> frames the commercial question -> defines opportunity
opportunity-decomposition: Demand, means, application, and benefit form the paper's opportunity test. -> identifies missing outputs -> commits to modeling
quantitative-commitment: A time-dependent private-firm model will test application and benefit. -> creates an inspectable objective -> methods type the alternatives

global_organization_chain: Only after the positive language, organization, model, and visual chain is complete does G7 record formula, unit, calibration, simulation, arithmetic, payoff, validation, and scope warnings.

moves: input: A debris-removal business question, two intervention classes, collision exposure, and a possible regulatory response.
rhetorical job: Compress the threat, firm role, three-model architecture, principal results, recommendation, and parameter caveat.
analytical job: Preview annual profit accounting, Gamma-grid collision simulation, three removal alternatives, three scenario families, and a policy game.
output: A conditional claim that a combined insurer-remover can find a commercial opportunity under declared rates and assumptions.
handoff: The executive summary expands each alternative and scenario before the main paper defines the machinery.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: The compact three-model promise and a private firm that both insures launches and removes debris.
rhetorical job: Expand the method, alternative, sensitivity, policy, and recommendation sequence without introducing equations.
analytical job: Distinguish land, space, and combined runs; lower-growth regulation; recyclable rockets; insurance-rate changes; and the payoff-matrix intervention.
output: A decision-facing comparison of commercial and regulatory conclusions.
handoff: The title and contents expose where each component is developed and reviewed.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: The executive summary's promised time-dependent evaluation, collision model, alternatives, scenarios, and game.
rhetorical job: Make the complete source order inspectable before technical details.
analytical job: Index methods, terminology, financial model, collision model, results, what-if scenarios, game theory, conclusions, improvements, and references.
output: A 23-page internal roadmap nested inside 26 physical PDF pages.
handoff: The introduction converts the physical problem into a four-part commercial-opportunity test.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: More than 500,000 debris pieces, collision damage, candidate removal technologies, and uneven costs and benefits.
rhetorical job: Turn a physical hazard into a measurable commercial-opportunity question for a private firm.
analytical job: Decompose opportunity into demand, means, application, and benefit; treat the last two as the unresolved modeling target.
output: A time-dependent profitability objective with named stakeholders and technologies.
handoff: Existing Methods classifies the technologies that later create removal costs and capacities.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: Laser Broom, Huff-and-Puff, Snagging and Moving, and Solar Sail proposals.
rhetorical job: Classify interventions by deployment location and compare operating mechanisms and practical limits.
analytical job: Separate fixed from recurring cost, working altitude, removal capacity, launch dependence, and collision or targeting risk.
output: Two alternative families used by the cost and debris-update models.
handoff: Terminology and notation define the financial and physical interfaces used to combine them.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: Insurance, compensation, utility, debris, launch, removal, probability, and game concepts.
rhetorical job: Stabilize terms and symbols before they cross the economic, simulation, and policy models.
analytical job: Define annual and cumulative income, two cost terms, commission, collision probability, debris state, removal quantities, and space-device capacity.
output: A typed interface for N_t, R_t, C_t, N_T, n_t, w, alpha, C_1t, C_2t, p_t, q_t, Pr(t), delta, Q_t, and epsilon.
handoff: Model One composes the financial quantities into revenue, cost, compensation, and profit.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: A 2016-2030 horizon, launch counts, satellite value, insurance rate, removal choices, collision probability, and compensation parameters.
rhetorical job: Make commercial opportunity measurable through annual and accumulated net income.
analytical job: Decompose income into premium revenue, removal cost, and collision compensation; derive compensation through a Cobb-Douglas construction.
output: N_t and N_T for any removal alternative once Pr(t) and removal quantities are supplied.
handoff: Model Two supplies the time-dependent collision probability and debris inventory.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: A three-dimensional orbital debris field and a need for a tractable collision-frequency simulation.
rhetorical job: Declare the physical reduction and distributional rationale before constructing a numerical field.
analytical job: Restrict the hazard to 1-10 cm debris, assume local uniformity and persistence, reduce the orbit to two dimensions, and select a Gamma radial family by visual similarity.
output: A two-dimensional radial representation with explicit but weakly calibrated assumptions.
handoff: The distribution section discretizes the representation into four rings and a binary matrix.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: A Gamma radial shape, four altitude layers, a 1000 by 1000 domain, and a hand-set occupancy rate.
rhetorical job: Convert the distributional story into a field that can be changed by removal, growth, and launches.
analytical job: Assign Gamma mass to rings, exclude the Earth and atmosphere, randomly fill about 15 percent of valid cells, and encode occupancy as zero or one.
output: A synthetic binary debris matrix.
handoff: The annual simulation processes remove cells, add debris, launch satellites, and count overlaps.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: The binary field, land and space working bands, debris growth, annual launches, and a same-cell collision rule.
rhetorical job: Order the physical and stochastic operations that generate the financial model's collision input.
analytical job: Randomly remove accessible debris, add linearly described but five-percent-recurring debris, grow launches from 110, count co-occupied cells, and normalize by launches.
output: Annual Q_t and Pr(t) paths for a removal scenario.
handoff: Results combine those paths with the corresponding removal-cost equations.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: A common 15-year horizon and three removal-cost and debris-update regimes.
rhetorical job: Compare alternatives on aligned profit and remaining-debris outputs before choosing one.
analytical job: Run land-only, space-only, and combined scenarios; interpret break-even behavior, inner-layer control, ending debris, and accumulated profit.
output: A recommendation for the combined alternative under the paper's parameter settings.
handoff: What-if sections perturb growth, reusable-launch lifetime, and insurance rate around that choice.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: The combined alternative and debris-growth settings of five, four, three, two percent plus a logarithmic trend.
rhetorical job: Translate lower growth into ending inventories and a bounded case for international regulation.
analytical job: Hold the model fixed, rerun the growth process, compare ending debris counts and marginal reductions, and interpret diminishing changes.
output: A local policy scenario linking stronger growth control with less ending debris.
handoff: The next scenario changes space-removal launch cost through reusable-rocket lifetime.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: The space-based cost structure and reusable-rocket lifetimes of three, six, nine, and twelve uses.
rhetorical job: Check whether a plausible launch technology change materially alters accumulated profit.
analytical job: Rerun the financial path for four lifetimes, compare maximum and minimum profit, and relate the limited effect to compensation liability.
output: A local claim that rocket reuse affects profit less than the dominant modeled costs.
handoff: The insurance-rate sweep changes the revenue and compensation interface directly.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: Insurance rates of three, four, five, and six percent under otherwise fixed simulation conditions.
rhetorical job: Connect the central business parameter to break-even timing and accumulated profit.
analytical job: Compare four profit paths, estimate the reported marginal profit and break-even shift, and infer a recommended rate range.
output: A local commission threshold claim, not a joint uncertainty or market-demand result.
handoff: Game theory then changes insurer and owner incentives through a policy payoff matrix.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: Satellite-owner insurance choices, firm removal choices, assumed complete information, and two 3 by 3 payoff matrices.
rhetorical job: Turn the commercial analysis into a strategic policy argument with inspectable equilibria.
analytical job: Enumerate strategies, check best responses in the baseline matrix, alter payoffs under policy, identify the new equilibrium, and compare both players' payoffs.
output: A policy-induced equilibrium shift that is Pareto-improving only within the supplied matrices.
handoff: Conclusions restate the commercial, rate, and policy decisions and then name model repairs.

moves: input: The three alternative runs, three scenario families, two payoff matrices, and the paper's own model assessment.
rhetorical job: Separate decision claims from claimed strengths and concrete future repairs.
analytical job: Restate commercial opportunity, combined removal, commission, standards, and regulation; then identify 3D geometry, resource allocation, and optimal-start-time extensions.
output: A capability-and-repair contract for transfer rather than an unconditional solution claim.
handoff: References expose the technology, launch, debris, distribution, cost, and policy provenance.

rhetorical job: Expose which external sources support context and inputs and what cannot be reproduced.
analytical job: Map eighteen citations to claims while recording missing retrieval freezes, datasets, parameters, code, seeds, run logs, and payoff derivations.
output: A provenance boundary rather than a complete reproduction package.

main_argument_chains.claim: Debris hazard and available interventions create a commercial question that is measured through a merged insurer-remover's fifteen-year income.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: measure the opportunity through a bounded private-firm accounting model

main_argument_chains.claim: Launch premiums, removal cost, collision frequency, and compensation form one typed handoff from physical state to annual and cumulative profit.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: keep physical collision output and financial loss connected through an explicit typed handoff

main_argument_chains.claim: A reduced Gamma ring field is changed by removal, growth, and launches before same-cell overlaps produce scenario-specific risk.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: produce scenario-specific risk paths while retaining calibration and grid boundaries

main_argument_chains.claim: Land, space, and combined alternatives share a horizon, profit metric, and debris metric before the conditional combined recommendation.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: choose the combined alternative only within the aligned scenario and metrics

main_argument_chains.claim: Growth, rocket lifetime, and commission reruns expose local response without establishing global robustness or market optimality.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: separate one-factor response from global robustness or market optimality

main_argument_chains.claim: Best responses support the equilibrium shift and within-matrix payoff improvement while payoff derivation and external welfare remain unresolved.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: retain the equilibrium calculation while bounding the welfare claim by unreported payoff derivation and policy costs

warnings.warning: Insurance alpha is explicitly arbitrary, w is equated to an unspecified fair value, and no market, loss, demand, or percent-convention calibration supports the premium-revenue equation.
The generic removal-cost sum multiplies p_t by q_t although p_t is alternately a catcher price or conduct cost and q_t is alternately debris capacity or conduct count; units and indexing conflict.

The compensation formula multiplies by epsilon even though the notation table defines epsilon as debris removed per space trapper; n_(t-1) is also not reconciled with exposure from surviving satellites.
The Cobb-Douglas construction sets x2=alpha*w and k=0.5 without economic estimation, leaves mu unidentified, and converts utility into compensation without a dimensional or actuarial justification.
The symbol alpha is reused for the insurance rate and Gamma shape, while Gamma parameters, fitted observations, ring boundaries, normalization, and goodness of fit are absent.

The printed debris update is self-referential Q_t=Q_t-(...) rather than a transition from Q_(t-1), and it omits the growth term described immediately afterward; it is retained verbatim rather than silently repaired.
The launch recurrence n_1=110 and n_t=1.05*n_(t-1) is reconstructed from prose; the plotted 2001-2015 series is not fitted to justify either 110 or five percent.

The law-of-large-numbers statement has no independent-run protocol, sample size, seed ledger, convergence plot, Monte Carlo error, confidence interval, or check that the simulated trials match the claimed probability.
The land equation adds initial cost C0 to C_1t without a one-time indicator, so the printed form can charge the initial investment every year rather than only at project start.
